new_camps.name: Glacier Lake
new_camps.why: Sits about 600 ft below the PCT at Chikamin Pass, which puts the summit scramble in one morning; the cost is a climb back up on the way out.
new_camps.capacity: A couple of decent sites near the lake, none large.
new_camps.notes: Parties from Mineral Creek camp just below the outlet, on dirt or bare rock. It is exposed and can be cold and windy overnight.

camps.name: Ridge Lake and Gravel Lake, PCT beyond Kendall Katwalk
camps.why: The first real water and tent sites on the PCT past the Katwalk, so a Snoqualmie Pass start puts you in range of the climb and out of the way of the long Mineral Creek approach.

camps.name: Park Lakes basin
camps.why: Camp for the other approach, up Mineral Creek on the east side; from the PCT start it is a detour, but it sits right under the southeast slopes.

plan_conflict: Park Lakes basin is on file as main, but this plan starts from the Snoqualmie Pass PCT trailhead and sleeps at Ridge Lake, so Ridge/Gravel Lake is main here.

camps.name: Chimney Glacier hanging basin — the big boulder bivy
camps.why: Puts the route's glacier approach about two hours away and has overhang space for a few bivy sacks; when it is taken, parties push higher to moraine spots near 5,400 ft.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: An easy flat first night for late starters or a four-day trip, but it leaves a steep brushy climb to the bivy basin before the long summit day.

camps.name: Chimney Glacier hanging basin — the big boulder bivy
camps.why: The standard high camp below the glacier toe, with a sheltered overhang; it leaves a short moraine and glacier walk to the base on summit day.

camps.name: Sunrise Knob
camps.why: Mapped at about 4,650 ft in the same basin below the glacier toe; an alternative bench when the boulder bivy is already taken by another party.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: A flat, easy night for parties that start late, but it adds a steep brushy climb to the high camp and lengthens summit day.

plan_conflict: Both the boulder bivy and Sunrise Knob are on file as main; only one can be main for night 1, so Sunrise Knob is changed to route.

camps.name: Chimney Glacier hanging basin — the big boulder bivy
camps.why: The usual high camp below the glacier toe, with sheltered bivy space under the boulder; summit day starts a short moraine walk from your tent.

camps.name: Sunrise Knob
camps.why: Mapped at about 4,650 ft in the same basin; an alternative when the boulder bivy is occupied, with the same short approach to the glacier.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: An easy flat first night with plenty of space, but it leaves the steep brushy climb to the glacier basin for the morning of the summit day.

plan_conflict: Both the boulder bivy and Sunrise Knob are on file as main; only one can be main for night 1, so Sunrise Knob is changed to route.

new_camps.name: Ridge Lake and Gravel Lake, PCT beyond Kendall Katwalk
new_camps.why: The established camp for this approach, a mile past the Katwalk, and the only reliable water on the crest; it splits Huckleberry's long approach into two days.
new_camps.water: Ridge Lake and Gravel Lake sit beside the trail.
new_camps.notes: Ridge Lake is about 150 ft below the PCT and Gravel Lake, the larger one, about 175 ft below it. Roughly seven miles from the Snoqualmie Pass trailhead.

camps.name: Ridge Lake and Gravel Lake, PCT beyond Kendall Katwalk
camps.why: The break point most parties use: water and flat sites about seven miles in, leaving a lighter summit day and a long walk out.

camps.name: Commonwealth Basin and Red Pond
camps.why: Sits under Lundin and Red Mountain instead, off this route's line; it is a camp for those peaks, not a night for Huckleberry.

camps.name: Alaska Lake and Joe Lake, Gold Creek
camps.why: Reached by the unmaintained Gold Creek trail from the freeway side; it is a brushy alternative that skips the PCT miles but not the bushwhack.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: Flat trail all the way and water at every site; camping near the PCT junction or Lemah Meadow leaves the brush and the glacier for summit day.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: Easy flat miles to sites by Pete Lake or along Lemah Creek; the creek-side sites save about three miles on summit day over staying at the lake.

camps.name: Williams Lake and the upper Middle Fork meadows below Dutch Miller Gap
camps.why: The first real camp up the valley, a long day in but only a short climb from the gap and the peak; lake and meadow sites give water and space.

camps.name: Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps.why: Staging camp at the end of the closed road; sleeping here shortens day one but adds about seven trail miles to the summit day.

camps.name: Waptus Lake, with Spade Lake above it
camps.why: The gentle eastern approach from Salmon la Sac; a pleasant first night but it adds a long climb to the gap before the peak.

camps.name: Summit Chief Valley gravel flats
camps.why: A flat gravel wash directly below the face, reached a short way off the trail; the climb and the descent both start and end at your tent.

camps.name: Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps.why: A lower option at the road end; it spares the cross-country day with a heavy pack but adds miles and gain to summit day.

camps.name: Peggys Pond
camps.why: The usual base: close under the glacier route and an easy descent to the car the same day. Expect mosquitoes in July and early August.

camps.name: Squaw Lake
camps.why: A lower stop 2.5 miles in with established sites; it melts out earlier than the pond, but it adds miles to summit day.

camps.name: East summit bivouac
camps.why: A flat spot just under the east summit; used by parties who go past the pond to escape insects, and a cold, dry night with no water.

camps.name: Peggy's Pond, below Cathedral Rock
camps.why: The pond is where this loop ends, not where it sleeps: you pass it on summit day on the way down to the trailhead.

camps.name: Hyas Lake and Upper Hyas Lake
camps.why: An easy low camp close to the trailhead for a three-day trip; it adds a long climb to Deception Pass and the lakes before the glacier.

plan_conflict: Night 1 is at Jade Lake (or Pea Soup Lake outlet) in this plan, and neither is on file; I found no verified elevation for either, so no main camp is listed for night 1.

camps.name: La Bohn Lakes, La Bohn Gap and the Chain Lakes benches
camps.why: Camps right under the gap, so summit day is a short scramble; the price is a longer, steeper first day with a snow slope to the gap.

camps.name: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
camps.why: Established lake sites about eight to nine miles in, lower and buggier; stopping here keeps day one easier but adds the gap climb to summit day.

camps.name: Money Creek and Miller River campgrounds, Foss River roadhead
camps.why: Car campgrounds for the night before an early trailhead start; useful for a Friday-night arrival, though the Foss River road has had delays.

plan_conflict: Both La Bohn Lakes and Necklace Valley are on file as main; only one can be main for night 1, so Necklace Valley is changed to route.

new_camps.name: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
new_camps.why: The established lake sites at the end of a nine-mile first day; a camp here leaves the gap climb and the ridge to summit day.
new_camps.permit: A wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead at no fee.
new_camps.notes: Jade Lake has established sites; Emerald and Opal are quieter. Campfires are not allowed.

new_camps.name: La Bohn Lakes, La Bohn Gap and the Chain Lakes benches
new_camps.why: A higher camp below the gap that cuts summit day short; it makes day one longer and steeper and is colder.
new_camps.notes: A party that reached the gap by the snow slope camped by the larger La Bohn lake.

new_camps.name: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
new_camps.why: Established lake sites at the end of the nine-mile first day; Emerald and Opal give quieter sites and a shorter push to the gap.
new_camps.permit: A wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead at no fee.
new_camps.notes: Jade Lake has established sites and gets buggy early. Campfires are not allowed.

camps.name: Rock benches above Overcoat Glacier
camps.why: The highest camp, at the base of the summit snow; it makes summit day short but means a hard, brushy carry up from the valley.

camps.name: Overcoat Lake
camps.why: A lower base reached after the same brush, with water; it saves some of the carry but adds climbing to summit day.

camps.name: Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps.why: The end of the bike ride and the last night before the car; it keeps the loaded carry short but makes day one a long ride and walk.

plan_conflict: Night 2 is spent near Bears Breast Tarns per the plan, which is not on file, and I could not confirm its elevation, so night 2 has no main camp; Overcoat Lake and the benches are both on file as main for night 1, so Overcoat Lake is changed to route.
